title: ZoomInfo Intent Data Alternatives: 7 Options Compared
summary: Seven ZoomInfo intent data alternatives compared by signal source and level, from Bombora and G2 to tools that flag accounts evaluating your competitors.
body_markdown:
## The short answer: pick by the signal you’re missing


ZoomInfo intent shows which accounts are researching topics you choose, right next to ZoomInfo’s contact data. Pick an alternative by what that leaves out for your team.


- **Topic research from a publisher co-op:** Bombora.
- **Research on software review sites:** G2 Buyer Intent.
- **Named people researching at tech buyers:** TechTarget Priority Engine.
- **Intent inside an enterprise ABM platform:** 6sense or Demandbase.
- **A cheaper database with intent included:** Apollo or Cognism.
- **Accounts, and the contacts at them, actively evaluating a named competitor:** Letterdrop.


Most of these can run alongside ZoomInfo, so switching intent sources doesn’t mean giving up its contact data.


## What ZoomInfo intent gives you, and where it stops


ZoomInfo’s Professional plan lists no intent. Buyer Intent signals and clusters start at Copilot Advanced, and real-time intent, custom intent signals and competitor alerts are listed at Copilot Enterprise. Streaming Intent is an add-on priced on the keywords and accounts you track. None of it has a published price.


ZoomInfo says it sources its signals monthly from over 90% of accessible US devices and matches them to companies through 210 million IP-to-organization pairings. It covers thousands of topics, at the account level and, in some plans, the person level.


Third-party write-ups disagree on where that data comes from. Some describe it as largely partner co-op data, others as ZoomInfo’s own collection plus bidstream. Ask your rep which sources feed the plan you’re quoted.


Reviews raise two limits:


- **IP matching gets thin.** Remote workers and shared networks are hard to tie to a company, so some accounts never light up.
- **A topic spike isn’t a buying decision.** The reader could be a competitor, a consultant or one of your own customers.


Sales leaders also tell us they struggle to prove it worked. Teams that trialed database or web-keyword intent often couldn’t show measurable lift. An account-level flag doesn’t tell a rep who to call, so whatever effect it had got lost.


One team we spoke with tried person-level intent to fix that. Volume was small and the method was a black box. Reps couldn’t see why a person was flagged, so they stopped trusting the flags.


## 7 ZoomInfo intent data alternatives


### 1. Bombora


Bombora runs a Data Co-op, with its own tag on member B2B publisher sites. It covers more than 25,300 intent topics and calls its data consent-driven. Signals are account-level, so contacts come from somewhere else. It suits teams feeding topic data into a CRM, ad platform or ABM tool they already run.


### 2. G2 Buyer Intent


G2 sells what buyers do on G2, Capterra, Software Advice and GetApp: category and product page views, comparisons and pricing page visits. The signal is account-level and close to a purchase, and it integrates with Salesforce. It helps most when your category gets real traffic on those sites.


### 3. Informa TechTarget Priority Engine


Priority Engine draws on 58M+ permissioned members across 220 media properties and works at the account and prospect level. For IT sellers, it names the people doing the research. If your buyers sit in finance, operations or sales, coverage drops.


### 4. 6sense


6sense collects most keyword intent from its own publisher network. Partner intent from review sites such as G2, TrustRadius and PeerSpot needs a separate subscription to each, and twelve Bombora topics are included. It identifies accounts, not individuals, and assigns buying stages. Plans are quote only; Vendr buyer data puts the median contract around $62,000 a year.


### 5. Demandbase


Demandbase sells account and buying-group intent inside its ABM platform, priced as a platform fee plus a flat fee per user. Its data page doesn’t say where the intent signals come from, so ask before you sign. It fits marketing teams that want ads, intent and sales views under one contract.


### 6. Apollo and Cognism


If ZoomInfo’s price is the problem, a cheaper database with intent bundled in may be enough. Apollo includes a limited number of intent topics depending on the plan, with self-serve pricing. Cognism’s intent is powered by Bombora and priced by quote. Both put intent on top of a contact database, the same design as ZoomInfo.


### 7. Letterdrop


Letterdrop identifies accounts, and the contacts at them, actively evaluating your competitors using public signals data, such as job posts, RFPs, 10-Ks, subprocessor lists, and public activity from prospects and competitors. It confirms competitor customers through job posts, RFPs and vendor documents, cross-checks flagged accounts against your CRM, and routes them there daily.


29% of accounts Letterdrop flags as High are still-winnable deals, versus about 3% of random accounts. Use it with ZoomInfo: ZoomInfo shows who is researching and how to reach them, and Letterdrop shows which accounts are already evaluating a competitor.


## Research intent vs evaluation signals


The first six options measure research. Sales leaders we talk to call keyword intent decent signal that still doesn’t show anyone at the account is taking vendor calls.


Research intent tells you which accounts are reading about a category. An evaluation signal tells you which accounts are evaluating which competitor, and who is involved.


Reps need the second answer. In a live deal, the intel that matters is which competitors the account is evaluating, who is doing the evaluating, and what those people care about. Then come the competitor’s pricing and where they’re stronger and weaker than you.


Discovery calls rarely surface this. Buyers keep their other evaluations to themselves, and “who else are you looking at?” on a first call gets a polite non-answer. Ideally you know which vendors are in the room before the buyer tells you.


## How to test an intent source before you sign


1. **Use one account list for every vendor.** Include accounts that became closed-won deals in the last two quarters, and count how many each source flagged before the opportunity opened.
2. **Ask for raw samples.** Get event type, date, account and, where offered, the contact for each signal. Ask how many of your target accounts showed any signal in the last 90 days.
3. **Set the bar at your current outbound.** One buyer we spoke with holds every paid source to the meeting rate their cold and warm sequences already get. Ask for a pilot that measures against it.
4. **Ask what each flag is based on.** Reps skip scores they can’t explain and work flags with a visible reason.
5. **Check what your ZoomInfo plan already includes.** Website visitors, intent topics and competitor alerts may already be in your tier. Don’t pay twice.


## Keep ZoomInfo intent, replace it, or stack it


Keep it if you already pay for the tier and your buyers research on the sites it covers. Having the signal on the contact record saves reps a step.


Replace it if signal volume in your category is too thin to act on, or the upgrade to an intent tier costs more than a standalone source. Run the same account-list test against a co-op source, a review-site source and an evaluation signal, and keep whichever produces accounts your reps will call.


The third option is to stack sources. One RevOps-led team we spoke with planned three layers: review-site intent for account research, database intent to watch competitor research, and an evaluation signal at the contact level. Accounts where the layers overlap get worked first, and when procurement contacts show up in the evaluation signal, the deal is late-stage and moves to the top of the list.


#### See which accounts are evaluating your competitors


Letterdrop finds the accounts, and the contacts at them, evaluating your competitors, and sends them to your CRM daily.
